#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Apply comprehensive tool title renaming - remove Zot prefixes and improve clarity"""

import re

# Define all title changes (old_title → new_title)
# For tools with no title, we'll add one
title_changes = {
    # Existing titles - remove parens and make cleaner
    "Ask Paper (Content Retrieval)": "Ask Paper",
    "Get Item Metadata": "Get Item",
    "Semantic Search (Content Discovery)": "Semantic Search",
    "Enhanced Semantic Search (Figure 3)": "Enhanced Semantic Search",
    "Search Items (Keyword Fallback)": "Search Items",
    "Search by Tag (Metadata Filter)": "Search by Tag",
    "Get Recent Items (Chronological)": "Get Recent Items",
    "Graph Search (Relationships)": "Graph Search",
    "Find Related Papers (Graph)": "Find Related Papers",
    "Find Seminal Papers (Graph)": "Find Seminal Papers",
    "Find Citation Chain (Graph)": "Find Citation Chain",
    "Find Collaborator Network (Graph)": "Find Collaborator Network",
    "Explore Concept Network (Graph)": "Explore Concept Network",
    "Track Topic Evolution (Graph)": "Track Topic Evolution",
    "Find Recent Developments (Temporal)": "Find Recent Developments",
    "Analyze Venues (Graph)": "Analyze Venues",
    "Literature Review (Workflow)": "Literature Review",
    # These are fine as-is (keep them)
    "Export to Markdown": "Export to Markdown",
    "Update Search Index": "Update Search Index",
}

# For tools that need new titles added (tool_name → new_title)
add_titles = {
    "zot_get_annotations": "Get Annotations",
    "zot_get_collection_items": "Get Collection Items",
    "zot_get_collections": "Get Collections",
    "zot_get_notes": "Get Notes",
    "zot_get_tags": "Get Tags",
    "zot_search_notes": "Search Notes",
    "zot_create_note": "Create Note",
    "zot_create_collection": "Create Collection",
    "zot_add_to_collection": "Add to Collection",
    "zot_remove_from_collection": "Remove from Collection",
    "zot_batch_update_tags": "Batch Update Tags",
    "zot_export_bibtex": "Export BibTeX",
    "zot_export_graph": "Export Graph",
    "zot_hybrid_vector_graph_search": "Hybrid Search",
    "zot_get_search_database_status": "Get Search Database Status",
    "fetch": "Fetch Web Content",
    "search": "Search Web",
}

with open('src/agent_zot/core/server.py', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

# Step 1: Replace existing titles
for old_title, new_title in title_changes.items():
    # Find and replace in annotations dict
    old_pattern = f'"title": "{re.escape(old_title)}"'
    new_pattern = f'"title": "{new_title}"'
    content = content.replace(old_pattern, new_pattern)
    if old_pattern in content:
        print(f"✓ Renamed: {old_title} → {new_title}")

# Step 2: Add titles to tools that don't have them
# This is trickier - need to find the decorator and add title annotation
for tool_name, new_title in add_titles.items():
    # Find the @mcp.tool decorator for this tool
    pattern = rf'(@mcp\.tool\([^)]*name="{re.escape(tool_name)}"[^)]*\))'
    
    match = re.search(pattern, content, re.DOTALL)
    if match:
        decorator = match.group(1)
        
        # Check if it already has a title (shouldn't, but check anyway)
        if '"title":' in decorator:
            continue
        
        # Check if it has an annotations dict
        if 'annotations=' in decorator:
            # Has annotations dict, add title to it
            # Find the annotations dict
            anno_pattern = r'(annotations=\s*\{[^}]*)'
            anno_match = re.search(anno_pattern, decorator)
            if anno_match:
                anno_dict = anno_match.group(1)
                # Add title before the closing }
                new_anno = anno_dict.rstrip()
                if new_anno.endswith(','):
                    new_anno += f'\n        "title": "{new_title}"'
                else:
                    new_anno += f',\n        "title": "{new_title}"'
                content = content.replace(anno_dict, new_anno)
                print(f"✓ Added title to {tool_name}: {new_title}")
        else:
            # No annotations dict, need to add one
            # Find where to insert it (after description, before closing paren)
            # Look for the pattern: description="...",\n)
            desc_end_pattern = rf'(name="{re.escape(tool_name)}",[^)]*description="[^"]*")([\s,]*\))'
            desc_match = re.search(desc_end_pattern, content, re.DOTALL)
            if desc_match:
                before_close = desc_match.group(1)
                close_paren = desc_match.group(2)
                # Add annotations dict
                new_decorator = before_close + ',\n    annotations={\n        "readOnlyHint": True,\n        "title": "' + new_title + '"\n    }' + close_paren
                content = content.replace(desc_match.group(0), new_decorator)
                print(f"✓ Added annotations with title to {tool_name}: {new_title}")

# Write back
with open('src/agent_zot/core/server.py', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)

print("\n✅ All tool titles updated!")
SCRIPT

    "zot_get_notes": "Zotero",
    "zot_create_note": "Zotero",
    "zot_search_notes": "Zotero",
    "zot_get_annotations": "Zotero",
    "zot_get_recent": "Zotero",
    "zot_search_items": "Zotero",
    "zot_export_bibtex": "Zotero",
    "zot_export_markdown": "Zotero",
    
    # System/indexing (uses Qdrant + Zotero)
    "zot_get_search_database_status": "System",
    "zot_update_search_database": "System",
    
    # Web tools
    "fetch": "Web",
    "search": "Web",
}

with open('src/agent_zot/core/server.py', 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

import re

# For each tool, find its current title and add backend label
for tool_name, backend in backend_map.items():
    # Find the @mcp.tool decorator for this tool
    pattern = rf'(@mcp\.tool\([^)]*name="{re.escape(tool_name)}"[^)]*)"title":\s*"([^"]+)"'
    
    match = re.search(pattern, content, re.DOTALL)
    if match:
        current_title = match.group(2)
        
        # Don't add if already has backend label
        if "(" in current_title and ")" in current_title:
            print(f"⏭️  {tool_name}: already has label - {current_title}")
            continue
        
        # Create new title with backend label
        new_title = f"{current_title} ({backend})"
        
        # Replace in content
        old_pattern = f'"title": "{current_title}"'
        new_pattern = f'"title": "{new_title}"'
        
        if old_pattern in content:
            content = content.replace(old_pattern, new_pattern, 1)
            print(f"✓ {tool_name}: {current_title} → {new_title}")
        else:
            print(f"❌ {tool_name}: Could not find exact title match for '{current_title}'")
    else:
        print(f"⚠️  {tool_name}: Could not find in decorators")

# Write back
with open('src/agent_zot/core/server.py', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)

print("\n✅ Backend labels added to all tool titles!")

import re

with open('src/agent_zot/core/server.py', 'r') as f:
    lines = f.readlines()

# Find all @mcp.tool decorators with full context
i = 0
tools = []
while i < len(lines):
    line = lines[i]
    
    if '@mcp.tool(' in line and not line.strip().startswith('#'):
        decorator_lines = []
        j = i
        paren_depth = 0
        while j < len(lines):
            decorator_lines.append(lines[j])
            paren_depth += lines[j].count('(') - lines[j].count(')')
            if paren_depth == 0 and ')' in lines[j]:
                break
            j += 1
        
        decorator_text = ''.join(decorator_lines)
        
        name_match = re.search(r'name="([^"]+)"', decorator_text)
        tool_name = name_match.group(1) if name_match else None
        
        title_match = re.search(r'"title":\s*"([^"]+)"', decorator_text)
        title = title_match.group(1) if title_match else "(no title)"
        
        if tool_name:
            tools.append((tool_name, title))
        
        i = j + 1
    else:
        i += 1

tools.sort()

print(f"✅ All {len(tools)} tools with backend labels:\n")
print(f"{'Tool Name':<42} {'Title with Backend':<60}")
print("="*102)

# Group by backend
qdrant_tools = []
neo4j_tools = []
hybrid_tools = []
zotero_tools = []
system_tools = []
web_tools = []

for name, title in tools:
    if "(Qdrant)" in title and "Neo4j" not in title:
        qdrant_tools.append((name, title))
    elif "(Neo4j)" in title and "Qdrant" not in title:
        neo4j_tools.append((name, title))
    elif "Qdrant+Neo4j" in title or ("Qdrant" in title and "Neo4j" in title):
        hybrid_tools.append((name, title))
    elif "(Zotero)" in title:
        zotero_tools.append((name, title))
    elif "(System)" in title:
        system_tools.append((name, title))
    elif "(Web)" in title:
        web_tools.append((name, title))
    else:
        print(f"⚠️  {name:<40} {title:<60}")

# Print grouped
print("\n🔵 QDRANT TOOLS (Semantic/Vector Search):")
for name, title in qdrant_tools:
    print(f"  {name:<40} {title}")

print("\n🟢 NEO4J TOOLS (Graph Operations):")
for name, title in neo4j_tools:
    print(f"  {name:<40} {title}")

print("\n🟣 HYBRID TOOLS (Qdrant + Neo4j):")
for name, title in hybrid_tools:
    print(f"  {name:<40} {title}")

print("\n🟡 ZOTERO TOOLS (Metadata/CRUD):")
for name, title in zotero_tools:
    print(f"  {name:<40} {title}")

print("\n🔴 SYSTEM TOOLS:")
for name, title in system_tools:
    print(f"  {name:<40} {title}")

print("\n⚪ WEB TOOLS:")
for name, title in web_tools:
    print(f"  {name:<40} {title}")

print(f"\n📊 Summary:")
print(f"   Qdrant: {len(qdrant_tools)}")
print(f"   Neo4j: {len(neo4j_tools)}")
print(f"   Hybrid: {len(hybrid_tools)}")

print(f"   Total: {len(tools)}")

import re

with open('src/agent_zot/core/server.py', 'r') as f:
    lines = f.readlines()

i = 0
tools = []
while i < len(lines):
    line = lines[i]
    if '@mcp.tool(' in line and not line.strip().startswith('#'):
        decorator_lines = []
        j = i
        paren_depth = 0
        while j < len(lines):
            decorator_lines.append(lines[j])
            paren_depth += lines[j].count('(') - lines[j].count(')')
            if paren_depth == 0 and ')' in lines[j]:
                break
            j += 1
        
        decorator_text = ''.join(decorator_lines)
        name_match = re.search(r'name="([^"]+)"', decorator_text)
        tool_name = name_match.group(1) if name_match else None
        title_match = re.search(r'"title":\s*"([^"]+)"', decorator_text)
        title = title_match.group(1) if title_match else "(no title)"
        
        if tool_name:
            tools.append((tool_name, title))
        i = j + 1
    else:
        i += 1

hybrid = [t for t in tools if "Qdrant+Neo4j" in t[1]]

chatgpt = [t for t in tools if "ChatGPT Compat" in t[1]]

  2341→def _extract_item_key_from_input(value: str) -> Optional[str]:

  2353→    # - bare <KEY>

  2355→        r"zotero://select/(?:library/)?items/([A-Za-z0-9]{8})",
  2356→        r"/items/([A-Za-z0-9]{8})(?:[^A-Za-z0-9]|$)",
  2357→        r"\b([A-Za-z0-9]{8})\b",
  2358→    ]

   271→
   272→#### Common Pitfalls to Avoid:
   273→
   274→❌ **DON'T** report progress based on Qdrant count alone (includes metadata)
   275→❌ **DON'T** assume parsing finished without checking log for "Batch complete"
   276→❌ **DON'T** forget to search backwards for stage transitions
   277→❌ **DON'T** use old/cached data - always fetch fresh data
   278→❌ **DON'T** skip the verification section - process status is critical
   279→
   280→## Project Overview
   281→
   282→Agent-Zot is a customized Zotero Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that provides semantic search capabilities over Zotero research libraries. Built on [zotero-mcp](https://github.com/54yyyu/zotero-mcp), it has been enhanced with:
   283→
   284→- **Qdrant vector database** for production-grade semantic search (replaces ChromaDB)
   285→- **Docling parser** for advanced PDF parsing with structure preservation
   286→- **Neo4j GraphRAG** for knowledge graph extraction from papers
   287→- **Hybrid search** combining dense and sparse (BM25) embeddings
   288→
   289→The server exposes 20+ MCP tools for searching, retrieving, and managing Zotero libraries, enabling LLMs to interact with research papers through semantic search and metadata queries.

   420→### Data Flow
   421→
   422→**Indexing Pipeline:**
   423→1. Zotero items fetched via API or local SQLite database (database/local_zotero.py)
   424→2. PDF attachments parsed with Docling V2 backend → hierarchical chunks with metadata (parsers/docling.py)
   425→   - 8 parallel workers, CPU-only processing, ~7-8 seconds per PDF average (476 PDFs/hour)
   426→   - Standard ThreadPoolExecutor with as_completed() for natural backpressure (no semaphore leaks)
   427→   - Fresh DoclingParser instance per PDF for thread safety
   428→   - Batch processing (200 items/batch) with automatic deduplication
   429→3. Chunks embedded via BGE-M3 model (sentence-transformers, 1024D, GPU-accelerated with batch_size=32)
   430→4. Dense + sparse (BM25) vectors stored in Qdrant (batch_size=500 for optimal throughput)
   431→5. [Optional] Neo4j knowledge graph extraction (clients/neo4j_graphrag.py, GPT-4o-mini)
   432→
   433→**Search Pipeline:**
   434→1. Query → BGE-M3 embedding (GPU-accelerated) + BM25 sparse vector
   435→2. Hybrid search in Qdrant (RRF fusion of dense semantic + sparse keyword matching)
   436→3. Cross-encoder reranking (ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2, GPU-accelerated) for quality boost
   437→4. Results filtered by metadata (item_key, doc_type, etc.)
   438→5. [Optional] Graph traversal for related concepts via Neo4j

   580→## Key Implementation Details
   581→
   582→### Semantic Search
   583→
   584→`semantic_search.py` implements two-phase indexing:
   585→
   586→1. **Metadata indexing** - Fast, includes title/abstract/notes
   587→2. **Full-text indexing** - Slower, uses Docling to parse PDFs
   588→
   589→Use `--extract-fulltext` flag to enable full-text parsing during updates.
   590→
   591→### Hybrid Search
   592→
   593→`qdrant_client_wrapper.py` implements hybrid search:
   594→
   595→- **Dense vectors** - OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (3072 dimensions)
   596→- **Sparse vectors** - BM25 with TF-IDF (10,000 features)
   597→- **Fusion** - RRF (Reciprocal Rank Fusion) to combine results
   598→
   599→### Docling Parser
   600→
   601→`docling_parser.py` uses HybridChunker with CPU-only processing:
   602→
   603→- **CPU-only mode:** Forced `device="cpu"` to avoid MPS GPU memory exhaustion with 8 parallel workers
   604→- **Performance:** 7.3x faster than GPU (35s vs 254s per PDF) due to parallel processing without memory contention
   605→- **Token-aware chunking:** Default 512 tokens aligned with BGE-M3 embeddings
   606→- **Structure preservation:** Respects document hierarchy (headings, sections)
   607→- **Table/formula parsing:** Disabled by default (`parse_tables=false`, `do_formula_enrichment=false`) for 4x speedup
   608→- **Conditional OCR:** Disabled by default (`fallback_enabled=false`), only enabled for scanned PDFs if configured
   609→- **8-worker parallelization:** Optimized for M1 Pro (8 performance cores)
   610→
   611→**GPU vs CPU Trade-off:**
   612→- **Embeddings (BGE-M3):** Still use MPS GPU for 5-10x faster batch processing (sequential, no contention)
   613→- **Docling parsing:** Use CPU for 7.3x faster processing (parallel, memory-bound workload)
   614→- **Result:** Best of both worlds - parallel CPU parsing + fast GPU embeddings
   615→
   616→### Local Mode
   617→
   618→When `ZOTERO_LOCAL=true`:
   619→
   620→- Direct SQLite access via `local_db.py` for faster indexing
   621→- No API rate limits
   622→- Requires local Zotero installation
   623→
   624→### Neo4j GraphRAG (Optional)
   625→
   626→**Purpose**: Extract knowledge graphs from research papers for relationship-aware search and discovery.
   627→
   628→#### Core Components
   629→
   630→1. **Client**: `src/agent_zot/clients/neo4j_graphrag.py`
   631→   - Config-driven schema (8 entity types, 12 relationship types)
   632→   - Free local LLM support via Ollama (Mistral 7B Instruct)
   633→   - Free local embeddings via SentenceTransformer (BGE-M3)
   634→   - OpenAI support (GPT-4o-mini + text-embedding-3-large)
   635→
   636→2. **Population Script**: `populate_neo4j_from_qdrant.py`
   637→   - Read-only Qdrant access (never modifies vector DB)
   638→   - Concurrent processing with asyncio (default: 4 parallel tasks)
   639→   - 6-9x performance improvement (73 hours → 10-12 hours for 2,411 papers)
   640→   - CLI flags: `--dry-run`, `--limit`, `--concurrency`
   641→
   642→#### Config-Driven Schema
   643→
   644→**Entity types** (configurable via `config.json`):
   645→1. **Person** - Authors, researchers, historical figures
   646→2. **Institution** - Universities, research labs, companies
   647→3. **Concept** - Abstract ideas, frameworks, paradigms
   648→4. **Method** - Techniques, algorithms, approaches
   649→5. **Dataset** - Benchmark datasets, corpora, collections
   650→6. **Theory** - Theoretical frameworks, models, hypotheses
   651→7. **Journal** - Publication venues, academic journals
   652→8. **Field** - Academic disciplines, research areas
   653→
   654→**Relationship types** (configurable via `config.json`):
   655→1. **AUTHORED_BY** - Paper → Person
   656→2. **AFFILIATED_WITH** - Person → Institution
   657→3. **USES_METHOD** - Paper/Study → Method
   658→4. **USES_DATASET** - Paper/Study → Dataset
   659→5. **APPLIES_THEORY** - Paper/Study → Theory
   660→6. **DISCUSSES_CONCEPT** - Paper → Concept
   661→7. **BUILDS_ON** - Paper → Paper
   662→8. **EXTENDS** - Work → Prior Work
   663→9. **RELATED_TO** - Generic relationship
   664→10. **CITES** - Paper → Paper
   665→11. **PUBLISHED_IN** - Paper → Journal
   666→12. **BELONGS_TO_FIELD** - Paper/Concept → Field

### 1. **The Three-Tier Search Hierarchy is Confusing**

**Problem:** You have three overlapping semantic search tools that users have to choose between:
- `zot_semantic_search` (Level 1, Figure 1)
- `zot_hybrid_vector_graph_search` (Level 2, Figure 2)  
- `zot_enhanced_semantic_search` (Level 3, Figure 3)

- All three do roughly the same thing (find papers), just with different enrichment strategies
- The "Figure 1/2/3" references are implementation details, not user-facing concepts
- Creates decision paralysis

**Recommendation:** **Collapse this into ONE primary tool with an optional parameter**

```python
@mcp.tool(name="zot_semantic_search")

    limit: int = 10,
    ...
):
```

**Rationale:**
- **Simpler mental model:** "I want to search semantically" → one tool
- **Progressive disclosure:** Advanced users can use `enrichment_level="enhanced"`

**Recommendation:** **Remove it entirely or make it truly invisible**

**Why:**
- If semantic search can't find something, keyword matching won't either (your corpus is the same)
- The "I know the exact title" use case is rare and can be handled by `zot_get_item(item_key)`
- Every time you present this tool, you risk users choosing the wrong one

**If you must keep it:**
- Rename to `zot_exact_title_lookup` to make the use case crystal clear
- Or add a parameter to `zot_semantic_search`: `exact_match=True`

---

### 3. **Neo4j Tools Have a Discoverability Problem**

**The situation:** 10 Neo4j graph tools, but your graph is "0.5% populated" (per global instructions line 132).

**This creates a terrible UX:**
1. User tries `zot_find_seminal_papers`
2. Gets "No seminal papers found"
3. User thinks: "This tool is broken" (not "Oh, the graph isn't populated yet")

**Recommendation:** **Add runtime detection and helpful errors**

```python
@mcp.tool(name="zot_find_seminal_papers")
def find_seminal_papers(...):
    # Check graph population percentage
    graph_status = get_graph_status()
    
    if graph_status.population_pct < 10:
        return """
        ⚠️ Neo4j graph is only {graph_status.population_pct}% populated.
        This tool needs more data to work effectively.
        
        Alternative: Use zot_semantic_search to find papers, then sort by:
        - Publication year (older = more foundational)
        - Citation count in metadata
        
        To populate the graph: [link to docs]
        """
```

**Better yet:** Make these tools **auto-degrade gracefully**:
- Try graph-based approach first
- If graph is empty/incomplete, fall back to semantic search with helpful messaging

## 🟡 **Moderate Issues** (Consider These)

### 4. **zot_get_item's include_fulltext=True is Dangerous**

**Problem:** This parameter retrieves THE ENTIRE PDF as markdown. For a 50-page paper, that's potentially 50,000+ tokens.

**Your own guidance says:**
```
⚠️ include_fulltext=True is RARELY needed - only for comprehensive summarization
```

If it's rarely needed, why is it so easy to accidentally trigger?

**Recommendation:** **Remove the parameter entirely**

**Rationale:**
- You already have `zot_ask_paper` for reading paper content (much better - it's targeted)
- Full-text extraction should go through Qdrant (chunked, searchable, fast)
- The "I want the whole paper" use case is covered by multiple `zot_ask_paper` calls with different questions

**If you insist on keeping it:**
- Add a hard limit (e.g., max 10,000 tokens) with truncation warning
- Require explicit confirmation: `really_get_fulltext=True` (makes it harder to trigger accidentally)

---

### 5. **The Zotero CRUD Tools are Noisy**

**You have 17 Zotero tools.** Most are fine, but some feel redundant:

**Consolidation opportunities:**

| Current Tools | Consolidated Alternative |
|---------------|--------------------------|
| `zot_get_collections`<br>`zot_get_collection_items` | `zot_collections(action="list")`<br>`zot_collections(action="get_items", collection_id=...)` |
| `zot_add_to_collection`<br>`zot_remove_from_collection` | `zot_manage_collection(action="add/remove", ...)` |
| `zot_create_note`<br>`zot_get_notes`<br>`zot_search_notes` | `zot_notes(action="create/get/search", ...)` |

**Rationale:**

- Consistent interface (actions as parameters, not separate functions)
- Easier to document ("For collections, use `zot_collections`")

**Counterargument:** This makes each tool more complex (action parameters add cognitive load).

**My take:** For CRUD operations (collections, tags, notes), consolidation makes sense because they're logically grouped. Don't consolidate search tools (those should stay separate because they're conceptually different).

These interfaces are envisioned to operate via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, forming the backbone of an agentic architecture where AI agents — powered by GraphRAG and orchestrated by the MCP server — enable autonomous, context-aware reasoning over complex operational data.

```
By integrating GraphRAG with AI copilots in this way, the architecture supports an agentic workflow that is capable of both proactive and reactive decision-making. The implementation includes a conceptual dual-mode consumption framework designed for flexible insight delivery through both structured dashboards for automated reporting and visualization, and through AI agent interfaces that support ad hoc, real-time querying and proactive notifications.

## Industry Trends

Agentic is a popular term in the RAG industry for 2024, with many media outlets declaring it the year of the agent, and agents significantly influence the LLM ecosystem. GraphRAG and LazyGraphRAG technology is now available through Microsoft Discovery, an agentic platform for scientific research built in Azure.

The research demonstrates applications in areas like Incident and Change Management (ICM), with practical use cases including classification, root cause analysis, and troubleshooting guide recommendations.
```

```
I found several relevant research sources on tool calling LLM agents and the specialization vs consolidation debate. Here's what the research shows:

## Specialization Approaches

The multi-agent framework has brought new possibilities and dimensions to tool learning by enabling the decomposition of complex tasks into specialized subtasks handled by dedicated agents.(no content)Research proposes decomposing the general multi-agent framework into three distinct roles: a planner, a caller, and a summarizer, with each role instantiated by a single LLM agent, with each agent specializing in its designated task and collaboratively interacting with other agents to fulfill the overarching goal.(no content)Different agents can focus on specific tasks or aspects of a problem, improving efficiency and effectiveness.(no content)Unlike traditional LLMs, LLM-based agents adopt a division of labor approach, breaking down complex tasks into multiple subtasks handled by specialized agents, this method can enhance task efficiency and improves the quality and accuracy of generated code.

## Problems Leading to Specialization

You might run into the following problems: agent has too many tools at its disposal and makes poor decisions about which tool to call next, context grows too complex for a single agent to keep track of, and there is a need for multiple specialization areas in the system (e.g. planner, researcher, math expert, etc.).

## Consolidation Approaches

Tools can consolidate functionality, handling potentially multiple discrete operations (or API calls) under the hood. For example, tools can enrich tool responses with related metadata or handle frequently chained, multi-step tasks in a single tool call.(no content)Tracking tool calls can help reveal common workflows that agents pursue and offer some opportunities for tools to consolidate.

## Industry Trends

These models will have a place as components within larger automated systems rather than standalone products. They're becoming specialized tools within outcome-delivery infrastructures – like motors in appliances rather than products you buy separately.

The research suggests both approaches have merit: specialization for complex multi-step tasks and improved decision-making, and consolidation for efficiency and reducing context complexity.
```

```
## Core Agentic RAG Design Patterns

Agentic AI design patterns are reusable architectural approaches for building enterprise-ready AI agents, describing how agents can be structured – task-oriented, collaborative, self-improving, retrieval-augmented (RAG), or orchestrated – to solve specific business challenges.

### Key Design Patterns for 2025

**1. ReAct (Reasoning and Acting)**
A ReAct agent is an AI agent built on the "reasoning and acting" framework, which combines step-by-step thinking with the ability to use external tools.(no content)The ReAct framework works much like how humans solve problems — by thinking, acting, and adjusting along the way, alternating between thoughts, actions, and observations to handle complex tasks.

**2. RAG Agent Pattern**
RAG agent enhances generative AI by retrieving relevant information from enterprise knowledge sources at runtime, grounding its responses in up-to-date, context-specific data, which makes this agentic AI design pattern more accurate and reliable for enterprise use.

**3. Self-Route Pattern**
Self Route is a design pattern in Agentic RAG systems where Large Language Models play an active role in deciding how a query should be processed, relying on the LLM's ability to self-reflect and determine whether it can generate an accurate response, routing the query to alternative methods if needed.

**4. Agentic RAG Architecture**
Teams exploring complex use cases like autonomous agents or tool-augmented workflows can experiment with Agentic RAG architecture, where retrieval and generation are dynamically interleaved with planning and action-taking.

## Best Practices for Implementation

**Modular Architecture:**
Follow a modular RAG pattern: Separate your retriever, generator, and orchestration logic for easier updates and debugging.

**Continuous Improvement:**
Agentic patterns address limitations by adding planning/query decomposition, conditional retrieval (decide if retrieval is needed, from which source), and self-reflection/corrective loops.

**Monitoring and Adaptation:**
Monitor precision and recall: Track how often retrieved content actually improves generation quality, and fine-tune retrieval on usage patterns to adapt the system over time to user behavior and domain trends.(no content)Leverage hybrid indexing: Blend semantic and keyword-based search for flexible and robust content retrieval.

## Key Components

The Retrieval System fetches relevant information from a knowledge base using techniques like indexing, query processing, and algorithms such as BM25 or dense embeddings, while the Generation Model, typically a fine-tuned LLM, converts the retrieved data into contextual embeddings and generates coherent responses.

## Enterprise Considerations

Most enterprises start with Task-Oriented Agents for high-volume, repeatable processes, and as maturity grows, they layer on collaborative, RAG, and orchestrator patterns.

These patterns are being implemented across industries for customer support, healthcare decision support, financial analysis, and knowledge management where complex multi-step reasoning is required.
```

```
Here are the key recommendations for AI agent tool design from the article:

Tool Specialization and Consolidation:
- Avoid creating too many tools or overly generic tools
- Consolidate related functionality into more purposeful tools
- Focus on tools that match natural human problem-solving approaches

Examples of Good Tool Design:
- Instead of separate `list_users`, `list_events`, `create_event` tools, create a single `schedule_event` tool
- Replace `read_logs` with `search_logs` that returns only relevant log lines
- Create `get_customer_context` instead of separate customer lookup tools

Tool Description and Naming Principles:
- Use clear, descriptive namespacing (e.g. `asana_projects_search`)
- Provide context that explains tool purpose and usage
- Make tool names reflect natural task subdivisions

Parameter and Response Design:
- Return high-signal, human-readable information
- Avoid cryptic technical identifiers
- Implement response format options (e.g. "concise" vs "detailed")
- Optimize for token efficiency

Error Handling:
- Provide actionable, specific error messages
- Steer agents toward correct tool usage
- Include examples of correct input formats
- Encourage more efficient search/query strategies

Key Quote: "Tools should enable agents to subdivide and solve tasks in much the same way that a human would."
```

```
   274→    def should_update_database(self) -> bool:
   275→        """Check if the database should be updated based on configuration."""
   276→        if not self.update_config.get("auto_update", False):
   277→            return False
   278→        
   279→        frequency = self.update_config.get("update_frequency", "manual")
   280→        
   281→        if frequency == "manual":
   282→            return False
   283→        elif frequency == "startup":
   284→            return True
   285→        elif frequency == "daily":
   286→            last_update = self.update_config.get("last_update")
   287→            if not last_update:
   288→                return True
   289→            
   290→            last_update_date = datetime.fromisoformat(last_update)
   291→            return datetime.now() - last_update_date >= timedelta(days=1)
   292→        elif frequency.startswith("every_"):
   293→            try:
   294→                days = int(frequency.split("_")[1])
   295→                last_update = self.update_config.get("last_update")
   296→                if not last_update:
   297→                    return True
   298→                
   299→                last_update_date = datetime.fromisoformat(last_update)
   300→                return datetime.now() - last_update_date >= timedelta(days=days)
   301→            except (ValueError, IndexError):
   302→                return False
   303→        
   304→        return False
```

## 2. Key Technical Concepts

- **MCP (Model Context Protocol)** - Anthropic's protocol for connecting AI assistants to data sources
- **FastMCP** - Python framework for building MCP servers with @mcp.tool decorators
- **Agentic RAG** - Retrieval-Augmented Generation where agents autonomously choose tools and orchestrate multi-step workflows
- **Three-backend architecture**: Qdrant (vector DB), Neo4j (knowledge graph), Zotero (metadata/CRUD)
- **Tool specialization vs consolidation** - Key design decision for agent systems
- **GraphRAG** - Microsoft's pattern combining knowledge graphs with RAG (Figure 1/2/3 patterns)
- **ReAct pattern** - Reasoning and Acting framework for agentic AI
- **Tool calling patterns** - How LLM agents select and chain tools
- **Graceful degradation** - Tools providing fallback behavior when dependencies unavailable
- **Hybrid search** - Dense (semantic) + sparse (BM25) vector search with RRF fusion
- **BGE-M3 embeddings** - 1024-dimensional embeddings for semantic search
- **Docling parser** - Advanced PDF parsing with HybridChunker

- Steps:

- More precise than hybrid_vector_graph_search (chunk-level vs paper-level)

- **Figure 1**: Pure vector search (no graph)
- **Figure 2**: Vector + paper-level graph enrichment

## Recommendations

### HIGH PRIORITY: Clarify zot_search_items vs Semantic Search

**Issue:** `zot_search_items` performs metadata-based keyword search (title/author/year), which overlaps with semantic search for some queries but serves different use cases.

**Recommendation:** Add clear differentiation in descriptions:
\```python
@mcp.tool(
    name="zot_search_items",
    description="🔍 METADATA keyword search (title, author, year, etc.) - Use when you have specific bibliographic criteria. For topic/content discovery, use zot_semantic_search instead."
)
\```

**Why Keep Both:**
- Agents can learn: keyword search for bibliographic queries ("papers by Smith from 2020")
- Semantic search for conceptual queries ("papers about transformers")
- This is efficient specialization, not redundancy

### MEDIUM PRIORITY: Neo4j Graceful Degradation

**Issue:** Some Neo4j tools don't gracefully degrade when graph is empty/unavailable.

**Recommendation:** Add helpful guidance in error messages:
\```python
if not self.neo4j_client:
    return {
        "results": [],
        "error": "Neo4j GraphRAG is not enabled",
        "suggestion": "Run 'zot_update_search_database' to populate the graph first, or use zot_semantic_search for content discovery."
    }
\```

**Files to Update:**
- `src/agent_zot/search/semantic.py` - Graph search methods
- All Neo4j tool wrappers in `src/agent_zot/core/server.py`

### LOW PRIORITY: Tool Sequencing Hints (Optional)

**Enhancement Idea:** Add workflow hints in tool descriptions for complex multi-step tasks.

**Example:**
\```python
@mcp.tool(
    name="zot_find_related_papers",
    description="Find papers related via knowledge graph entities. For best results: (1) First use zot_semantic_search to find a relevant paper, (2) Then use this tool with that paper's item_key."
)
\```

**Benefits:**
- Helps agents learn optimal tool chaining
- Reduces trial-and-error in complex workflows

**Trade-off:**
- Adds verbosity to descriptions
- Agents may learn patterns through experience anyway

**Decision:** OPTIONAL - Monitor agent behavior first to see if needed.

---

## Final Verdict

### Current Architecture: A (Excellent)

**Strengths:**
1. ✅ Implements industry-standard GraphRAG patterns (Qdrant Figure 1/2/3)
2. ✅ Tool specialization matches distinct analytical workflows
3. ✅ Clear separation of concerns across backends
4. ✅ Graceful degradation in hybrid tools
5. ✅ Modular design supports agentic tool selection

**Justified Design Decisions:**
- Three semantic search tools = Three GraphRAG patterns (not redundancy)
- Separate CRUD operations = Clear intent for agents (not over-engineering)
- Neo4j specialization = Distinct graph queries (not consolidation opportunity)

**Minor Improvements Available:**
1. Clarify zot_search_items vs semantic search in descriptions (5 min fix)
2. Add Neo4j error message guidance (15 min fix)
3. Optional: Tool sequencing hints (30 min enhancement)

### Comparison to Industry Standards

| Best Practice | Agent-Zot Implementation | Grade |

## Evidence-Based Recommendation: **SPLIT THEM BACK**

After validating against agentic RAG best practices, I now recommend **reversing the consolidation**.

### Why Split (Aligned with My Search Tool Analysis)

**1. Token Cost Control**
- Metadata: ~500 tokens
- Full text: 10k-100k tokens (20-200x more expensive)
- Agents may not understand the cost implications of `include_fulltext=True`

**2. Matches "Different Workflows" Principle**
Just like I validated that the three search tools are distinct patterns:
- `zot_get_metadata` = Quick bibliographic lookup
- `zot_get_fulltext` = Deep content analysis
- These are **different retrieval patterns**, not parameter variations

**3. Clear Intent for Agents**
- Tool name signals intent clearly
- Prevents accidental expensive operations
- Agents can learn: "Check metadata first, then fetch fulltext if relevant"

**4. Anthropic Guidelines Alignment**
The example from Anthropic was consolidating `list_users` + `create_event` into `schedule_event` because they're **steps in one workflow**.

But `get_metadata` → `get_fulltext` is a **conditional workflow**: 
- Always get metadata first
- Only get fulltext if needed (minority of cases)

This matches the three search tools being separate: different use cases, different cost profiles.

### Recommended Structure

```python
@mcp.tool(
    name="zot_get_item",
    description="🟡 Get Zotero item METADATA (title, authors, year, abstract, etc.). Fast and lightweight. For full PDF text, use zot_ask_paper instead.",
    annotations={"title": "Get Item (Zotero)"}
)
def get_item(item_key: str, include_abstract: bool = True, format: str = "markdown"):
    # Metadata only - no fulltext option
    pass

@mcp.tool(
    name="zot_get_item_fulltext",
    description="📄 Get FULL PDF TEXT of a Zotero item. WARNING: Expensive operation (10k-100k tokens). Use zot_get_item first to verify relevance. For Q&A, use zot_ask_paper instead.",
    annotations={"title": "Get Item Full Text (Zotero)"}
)
def get_item_fulltext(item_key: str):
    # Full text retrieval only
    pass
```

**Key improvement:** Deprecate `zot_get_item_fulltext` in favor of `zot_ask_paper` for most use cases. The only time you need raw fulltext is for export/analysis, not Q&A.

### Final Recommendation

**Yes, I still recommend separation** - even more strongly after the evidence-based analysis. This aligns with the principle that guided keeping three separate search tools: **distinct retrieval patterns deserve distinct tools in agentic systems**.

# Agent-Zot Final Architecture Recommendations
## Evidence-Based Comprehensive Assessment

**Date:** 2025-10-21

## Executive Summary

- ✅ Anthropic MCP tool design guidelines
- ✅ Qdrant GraphRAG official documentation
- ✅ Microsoft GraphRAG research

## PRIORITY 1: Split zot_get_item (REQUIRED)

### Issue
`zot_get_item` currently has `include_fulltext` parameter that dramatically changes behavior:
- **Metadata only:** ~500 tokens, fast
- **With fulltext:** 10k-100k tokens (20-200x more expensive), slow

### Evidence-Based Rationale

**1. Different Retrieval Patterns (Not Parameter Variations)**
- Metadata retrieval = Quick bibliographic lookup
- Fulltext retrieval = Deep content analysis
- These are **fundamentally different workflows**, just like the three search tools

**2. Token Cost Control**
- Agents may not understand the cost implications of boolean flags
- Explicit tool names signal cost: `zot_get_item` vs `zot_get_fulltext`
- Prevents accidental expensive operations

**3. Anthropic Guidelines Alignment**
> "Tools should enable agents to subdivide and solve tasks in much the same way that a human would"

Human workflow:
1. Check metadata first (cheap, fast)
2. Only fetch fulltext if relevant (conditional, expensive)

This matches keeping search tools separate, not consolidating them.

**4. Better Tool Exists**
`zot_ask_paper` is **already the right tool** for content retrieval:
- Targeted chunk retrieval (more efficient)
- Semantic search within document
- No need for raw fulltext in most cases

### Recommended Implementation

**Option A: Remove include_fulltext Entirely (RECOMMENDED)**
\```python
@mcp.tool(
    name="zot_get_item",
    description="Get bibliographic metadata for a Zotero item (title, authors, abstract, etc.).\n\n⚠️ For paper CONTENT, use zot_ask_paper instead (more efficient).\n\nUse for: Bibliographic info, citations, metadata",
    annotations={"title": "Get Item (Zotero)"}
)
def get_item(
    item_key: str,
    include_children: bool = True,
    include_abstract: bool = True,
    format: str = "markdown"
):
    # NO include_fulltext parameter
    pass
\```

**Reasoning:**
- `zot_ask_paper` handles content retrieval better (semantic chunks)
- Raw fulltext is rarely needed (only for comprehensive summarization)
- Simplifies tool interface

**Option B: Create Separate Tool (If Raw Fulltext Needed)**
\```python

    name="zot_get_item_fulltext",
    description="⚠️ WARNING: Expensive operation (10k-100k tokens). Get raw full PDF text of a Zotero item.\n\n💡 For Q&A or content analysis, use zot_ask_paper instead (more efficient, targeted retrieval).\n💡 Only use this for comprehensive summarization when multiple zot_ask_paper calls aren't sufficient.\n\nUse for: Complete text export, comprehensive summarization",
    annotations={"title": "Get Item Full Text (Zotero)"}
)

**Recommendation:** **Option A** (remove parameter) unless you have evidence that raw fulltext is frequently needed.

## PRIORITY 2: Validate Three Search Tools (CONFIRMED ✅)

### Analysis
After reading implementation code (semantic.py lines 1323-1643), confirmed:

**1. `zot_semantic_search` (Line 1323) - Figure 1 Pattern**
- Pure Qdrant vector search
- Returns: similarity-ranked papers
- Use case: Fast discovery

**2. `zot_hybrid_vector_graph_search` (Line 1457) - Figure 2 Pattern**
- Vector search → find related papers via graph → boost by centrality
- Returns: papers + related_papers_count + combined_score
- Use case: Find influential/connected papers

**3. `zot_enhanced_semantic_search` (Line 1526) - Figure 3 Pattern**
- Vector search → extract point IDs → query Neo4j for chunk entities
- Returns: papers + chunk_entities + entity_types
- Use case: Entity-aware discovery

### Verdict: **KEEP ALL THREE** ✅

**Evidence:**
- Implements official Qdrant GraphRAG Figure 1/2/3 patterns
- Each returns **different data structures** with different value
- Matches Anthropic's "subdivide tasks like humans" principle
- Tool specialization improves agent efficiency (research-validated)

**No changes needed.**

```python
@mcp.tool(
    name="zot_get_item",
    description="Get bibliographic metadata for a Zotero item (title, authors, journal, abstract, DOI, etc.) plus list of child items (attachments, notes).\n\n⚠️ For paper CONTENT analysis, use zot_ask_paper instead (more efficient, targeted chunk retrieval).\n⚠️ For raw full PDF text, use zot_get_item_fulltext (expensive operation).\n\nReturns:\n- Bibliographic metadata (title, authors, year, journal, DOI)\n- Abstract (if available)\n- List of child items (attachments, notes)\n- Tags, collections\n\n~500-800 tokens, fast.\n\nUse for: Bibliographic information, citations, checking what attachments exist",
    annotations={
        "readOnlyHint": True,
        "title": "Get Item (Zotero)"
    }
)
def get_item(
    item_key: str,
    include_children: bool = True,
    include_abstract: bool = True,
    format: str = "markdown",
    *,
    ctx: Context
) -> str:
    """
    Get complete bibliographic metadata for a Zotero item.
    
    Args:
        item_key: Zotero item key/ID
        include_children: Whether to include child items like attachments and notes (default: True)
        include_abstract: Whether to include abstract in metadata (default: True)
        format: Output format - "markdown" or "bibtex" (default: "markdown")
        ctx: MCP context
        
    Returns:
        Comprehensive item metadata with child items list
    """
    try:
        # Validate format parameter
        if format not in ["markdown", "bibtex"]:
            return f"Error: Invalid format '{format}'. Must be 'markdown' or 'bibtex'"
            
        ctx.info(f"Fetching metadata for item {item_key}")
        zot = get_zotero_client()
        
        # Get the main item
        item = zot.item(item_key)
        if not item:
            return f"No item found with key: {item_key}"
            
        # For BibTeX format, just return BibTeX
        if format == "bibtex":
            return generate_bibtex(item)
            
        # Build markdown output
        output_parts = []
        
        # 1. Metadata section
        metadata = format_item_metadata(item, include_abstract)
        output_parts.append(metadata)
        
        # 2. Children section (if requested)
        if include_children:
            children = zot.children(item_key)
            if children:
                output_parts.append("\n---\n\n## Child Items\n")
                
                # Group by type
                attachments = [c for c in children if c.get("data", {}).get("itemType") == "attachment"]
                notes = [c for c in children if c.get("data", {}).get("itemType") == "note"]
                
                if attachments:
                    output_parts.append("\n### Attachments\n")
                    for att in attachments:
                        data = att.get("data", {})
                        title = data.get("title", "Untitled")
                        content_type = data.get("contentType", "unknown")
                        output_parts.append(f"- **{title}** ({content_type}) - Key: {att.get('key', 'N/A')}")
                
                if notes:
                    output_parts.append(f"\n### Notes ({len(notes)})\n")
                    for note in notes[:3]:  # Show first 3
                        note_text = note.get("data", {}).get("note", "")
                        preview = note_text[:100] + "..." if len(note_text) > 100 else note_text
                        output_parts.append(f"- {preview}")
                    if len(notes) > 3:
                        output_parts.append(f"- ... and {len(notes) - 3} more notes")
        
        return "\n".join(output_parts)
        
    except Exception as e:
        ctx.error(f"Error fetching item: {str(e)}")
        return f"Error fetching item: {str(e)}"
```

**Tool 2: Full Text (Expensive Fallback)**
```python
@mcp.tool(
    name="zot_get_item_fulltext",
    description="⚠️ EXPENSIVE FALLBACK (10,000-100,000 tokens) - Get complete raw PDF text from a Zotero item.\n\n💡 Try these MORE EFFICIENT options FIRST:\n- zot_ask_paper(item_key, question) → Retrieves relevant text chunks for Q&A (recommended)\n- zot_semantic_search(query) → Find papers by content/topic\n- zot_get_item(item_key) → Get metadata only\n\n✅ Use this ONLY when you need:\n- Comprehensive full-paper summarization (entire document context)\n- Semantic search failed but you know paper is relevant\n- Non-semantic tasks (word count, extract all references, find all equations)\n- Complete text export for external processing\n- Absoluteness > relevance (need ALL methodology, not excerpts)\n\n⚠️ WARNING: Returns 10k-100k tokens. Cost is 20-200x higher than zot_get_item.\n\nReturns:\n- All metadata (same as zot_get_item)\n- Complete extracted PDF text\n- Processing may take 10-30 seconds\n\nUse for: Complete text retrieval when targeted tools insufficient",
    annotations={
        "readOnlyHint": True,
        "title": "Get Item Full Text (Zotero)"
    }
)
def get_item_fulltext(
    item_key: str,
    *,
    ctx: Context
) -> str:
    """
    Get the full text content of a Zotero item.
    
    WARNING: This is an expensive operation that can return 10k-100k tokens.
    Consider using zot_ask_paper for targeted content retrieval instead.
    
    Args:
        item_key: Zotero item key/ID
        ctx: MCP context
        
    Returns:
        Markdown-formatted item metadata + complete full text
    """
    try:
        ctx.info(f"Fetching full text for item {item_key} (this may take a while)")
        zot = get_zotero_client()
        
        # First get the item metadata
        item = zot.item(item_key)
        if not item:
            return f"No item found with key: {item_key}"
            
        # Get item metadata in markdown format
        metadata = format_item_metadata(item, include_abstract=True)
        
        # Try to get attachment details
        attachment = get_attachment_details(zot, item)
        if not attachment:
            return f"{metadata}\n\n---\n\n⚠️ No suitable PDF attachment found for this item.\n\n💡 Suggestion: Use zot_get_item to verify attachments exist."
            
        ctx.info(f"Found attachment: {attachment.key} ({attachment.content_type})")
        
        # Try fetching full text from Zotero's full text index first
        try:
            full_text_data = zot.fulltext_item(attachment.key)
            if full_text_data and "content" in full_text_data and full_text_data["content"]:
                ctx.info("Successfully retrieved full text from Zotero's index")
                return f"{metadata}\n\n---\n\n## Full Text\n\n{full_text_data['content']}"
        except Exception as fulltext_error:
            ctx.info(f"Zotero index unavailable, will parse PDF: {str(fulltext_error)}")
        
        # Fallback: Download and parse PDF
        ctx.info(f"Downloading and parsing PDF for {attachment.key}...")
        
        # Download the file to a temporary location
        import tempfile
        import os
        from pathlib import Path
        
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False, suffix=".pdf") as tmp_file:
            tmp_path = tmp_file.name
            
        try:
            # Download file
            zot.dump(attachment.key, path=tmp_path)
            
            # Extract text from PDF
            from agent_zot.parsers.docling_parser import DoclingParser
            parser = DoclingParser()
            
            parsed_doc = parser.parse_document(Path(tmp_path))
            if parsed_doc and parsed_doc.full_text:
                ctx.info(f"Successfully extracted {len(parsed_doc.full_text)} characters from PDF")
                return f"{metadata}\n\n---\n\n## Full Text (Extracted from PDF)\n\n{parsed_doc.full_text}"
            else:
                return f"{metadata}\n\n---\n\n⚠️ Could not extract text from PDF. File may be scanned/image-based.\n\n💡 Suggestion: Try zot_ask_paper if this paper was indexed successfully."
                
        finally:
            # Clean up temp file
            if os.path.exists(tmp_path):
                os.unlink(tmp_path)
                
    except Exception as e:
        import traceback
        ctx.error(f"Error fetching full text: {str(e)}")
        ctx.error(f"Traceback: {traceback.format_exc()}")
        return f"Error fetching full text: {str(e)}\n\n💡 Suggestion: Use zot_ask_paper or zot_semantic_search instead."
```

```
@mcp.tool(
    name="zot_get_item",
    description="⚪ Get bibliographic metadata for a Zotero item (title, authors, journal, abstract, DOI, etc.). Returns metadata + child items by default.\n\n⚠️ For paper content analysis, use zot_ask_paper() instead (more efficient, targeted chunk retrieval).\n⚠️ include_fulltext=True is RARELY needed - only for comprehensive summarization when multiple zot_ask_paper() calls aren't sufficient.\n\nUse for: Bibliographic information, citations, metadata. For content: use zot_ask_paper() instead",
    annotations={
        "readOnlyHint": True,
        "title": "Get Item (Zotero)"
    }
)
def get_item(
    item_key: str,
    include_fulltext: bool = False,
    include_children: bool = True,
    include_abstract: bool = True,
    format: str = "markdown",
    *,
    ctx: Context
) -> str:
    """
    Get complete information about a Zotero item in a single call.
    Args:
        item_key: Zotero item key/ID
        include_fulltext: Whether to fetch and include full PDF text (slow, default: False)
        include_children: Whether to include child items like attachments and notes (default: True)
        include_abstract: Whether to include abstract in metadata (default: True)
        format: Output format - "markdown" or "bibtex" (default: "markdown")
        ctx: MCP context
    Returns:
        Comprehensive item information in specified format
    """
    try:
        # Validate format parameter
        if format not in ["markdown", "bibtex"]:
            return f"Error: Invalid format '{format}'. Must be 'markdown' or 'bibtex'"
        ctx.info(f"Fetching complete item data for {item_key}")
        zot = get_zotero_client()
        # Get the main item
        item = zot.item(item_key)
        if not item:
            return f"No item found with key: {item_key}"
        # For BibTeX format, just return BibTeX (no other sections)
        if format == "bibtex":
            return generate_bibtex(item)
        # Build comprehensive markdown output
        output_parts = []
        # 1. Metadata section
        metadata = format_item_metadata(item, include_abstract)
        output_parts.append(metadata)
        # 2. Children section (if requested)
        if include_children:
            try:
                children = zot.children(item_key)
                if children:
                    output_parts.append("\n---\n\n## Attachments & Notes")
                    # Group children by type
                    attachments = [c for c in children if c.get("data", {}).get("itemType") == "attachment"]
                    notes = [c for c in children if c.get("data", {}).get("itemType") == "note"]
                    # Format attachments
                    if attachments:
                        output_parts.append("\n### Attachments")
                        for i, att in enumerate(attachments, 1):
                            data = att.get("data", {})
                            title = data.get("title", "Untitled")
                            key = att.get("key", "")
                            content_type = data.get("contentType", "Unknown")
                            filename = data.get("filename", "")
                            output_parts.append(f"\n{i}. **{title}**")
                            output_parts.append(f"   - Key: {key}")
                            output_parts.append(f"   - Type: {content_type}")
                            if filename:
                                output_parts.append(f"   - Filename: {filename}")
                    # Format notes
                    if notes:
                        output_parts.append("\n### Notes")
                        for i, note in enumerate(notes, 1):
                            data = note.get("data", {})
                            key = note.get("key", "")
                            note_text = data.get("note", "")
                            # Clean up HTML in notes
                            note_text = note_text.replace("<p>", "").replace("</p>", "\n\n")
                            note_text = note_text.replace("<br/>", "\n").replace("<br>", "\n")
                            # Limit note length for display
                            if len(note_text) > 500:
                                note_text = note_text[:500] + "...\n\n(Note truncated)"
                            output_parts.append(f"\n{i}. Note (Key: {key})")
                            output_parts.append(f"\```\n{note_text}\n\```")
            except Exception as children_error:
                ctx.info(f"Could not fetch children: {str(children_error)}")
        # 3. Full text section (if requested)
        if include_fulltext:
            try:
                attachment = get_attachment_details(zot, item)
                if attachment:
                    ctx.info(f"Found attachment: {attachment.key} ({attachment.content_type})")
                    # Try fetching from Zotero's full text index first
                    try:
                        full_text_data = zot.fulltext_item(attachment.key)
                        if full_text_data and "content" in full_text_data and full_text_data["content"]:
                            ctx.info("Successfully retrieved full text from Zotero's index")
                            output_parts.append("\n---\n\n## Full Text\n\n" + full_text_data['content'])
                    except Exception:
                        # Try to download and convert the file
                        ctx.info(f"Attempting to download and convert attachment {attachment.key}")
                        import tempfile
                        import os
                        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
                            file_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, attachment.filename or f"{attachment.key}.pdf")
                            zot.dump(attachment.key, filename=os.path.basename(file_path), path=tmpdir)
                            if os.path.exists(file_path):
                                ctx.info(f"Downloaded file to {file_path}, converting to markdown")
                                converted_text = convert_to_markdown(file_path)
```

```
@mcp.tool(
    name="zot_get_tags",
    description="Get all tags used in your Zotero library.\n\nUse for: Exploring tag vocabulary and frequency across library",
    annotations={
        "readOnlyHint": True,
        "title": "Get Tags (Zotero)"
    }
)
def get_tags(
    limit: Optional[int] = None,
    *,
    ctx: Context
) -> str:
    """
    Get all tags used in your Zotero library.
    
    Args:
        limit: Maximum number of tags to return
        ctx: MCP context
    
    Returns:
        Markdown-formatted list of tags
    """
    try:
        ctx.info("Fetching tags")
        zot = get_zotero_client()
        
        
        tags = zot.tags(limit=limit)
        if not tags:
            return "No tags found in your Zotero library."
        
        # Format tags as markdown
        output = ["# Zotero Tags", ""]
        
        # Sort tags alphabetically
        sorted_tags = sorted(tags)
        
        # Group tags alphabetically
        current_letter = None
        for tag in sorted_tags:
            first_letter = tag[0].upper() if (tag and len(tag) > 0) else "#"
            
            if first_letter != current_letter:
                current_letter = first_letter
                output.append(f"## {current_letter}")
            
            output.append(f"- `{tag}`")
        
        return "\n".join(output)
    
    except Exception as e:
        ctx.error(f"Error fetching tags: {str(e)}")
        return f"Error fetching tags: {str(e)}"
```

\```python
@mcp.tool(
    name="zot_find_similar_papers",
    description="Find papers similar to a given paper using content-based vector similarity (More Like This query).

Uses the paper's actual document embedding to find semantically similar papers. More accurate than semantic_search(abstract) because it uses the full document vector.

💡 Different from zot_find_related_papers:
- THIS TOOL: Content similarity via Qdrant vectors (what the paper discusses)
- find_related_papers: Graph relationships via Neo4j (who/what it cites, shared authors)

Use when:
✓ 'Find papers similar to this one'
✓ 'More papers like ABC123'
✓ 'Papers with similar methodology/approach'

NOT for:
✗ 'Papers citing this' → use zot_find_citation_chain
✗ 'Papers by same author' → use zot_find_collaborator_network

Use for: Content-based 'More Like This' discovery using document vectors",
    annotations={
        "readOnlyHint": True,
        "title": "Find Similar Papers (Qdrant)"
    }
)
def find_similar_papers(
    item_key: str,
    limit: int = 10,
    *,
    ctx: Context
) -> str:
    """
    Find papers similar to the given paper using vector similarity.

    Args:
        item_key: Zotero item key of the reference paper
        limit: Maximum number of similar papers to return (default: 10)
        ctx: MCP context

    Returns:
        Markdown-formatted list of similar papers with similarity scores
    """
    try:
        from pathlib import Path
        from agent_zot.search.semantic import create_semantic_search

        config_path = Path.home() / ".config" / "agent-zot" / "config.json"
        search = create_semantic_search(str(config_path))

        if not search or not search.qdrant_client:
            return "Semantic search is not initialized. Please run 'agent-zot update-db' first."

        ctx.info(f"Finding papers similar to {item_key}")

        # Use Qdrant's recommend/similar query
        # This finds documents with similar vectors to the given document
        results = search.qdrant_client.recommend_similar(
            item_key=item_key,
            limit=limit
        )

        if not results or not results.get("results"):
            # Fallback: Get the item and use its abstract for search
            ctx.info("Direct similarity query unavailable, using abstract-based search as fallback")
            zot = get_zotero_client()
            item = zot.item(item_key)

            if not item:
                return f"No item found with key: {item_key}"

            abstract = item.get("data", {}).get("abstractNote", "")
            if not abstract:
                return f"Item {item_key} has no abstract for similarity search.\\n\\n💡 Suggestion: Use zot_find_related_papers for graph-based relationships instead."

            # Use semantic search with the abstract
            fallback_results = search.search(query=abstract, limit=limit)
            results = fallback_results

        # Format results
        output = [f"# Papers Similar to: {item_key}", ""]

        if "results" in results and results["results"]:
            for i, paper in enumerate(results["results"], 1):
                title = paper.get("title", "Untitled")
                authors = paper.get("creators_str", "Unknown authors")
                year = paper.get("year", "N/A")
                key = paper.get("item_key", "")
                score = paper.get("similarity_score", 0.0)

                output.append(f"## {i}. {title}")
                output.append(f"**Authors:** {authors}")
                output.append(f"**Year:** {year}")
                output.append(f"**Item Key:** `{key}`")
                output.append(f"**Similarity:** {score:.3f}")

                # Include abstract preview if available
                abstract = paper.get("abstract", "")
                if abstract:
                    preview = abstract[:200] + "..." if len(abstract) > 200 else abstract
                    output.append(f"**Abstract:** {preview}")

                output.append("")

            output.append(f"\\n**Total found:** {len(results['results'])}")
        else:
            output.append("No similar papers found.")
            output.append("\\n💡 Try:")
            output.append("- zot_semantic_search for topic-based discovery")
            output.append("- zot_find_related_papers for graph-based relationships")

        return "\\n".join(output)

    except Exception as e:
        import traceback
        ctx.error(f"Error finding similar papers: {str(e)}")
        ctx.error(f"Traceback: {traceback.format_exc()}")
        return f"Error finding similar papers: {str(e)}"
\```

**Note:** This implementation assumes Qdrant client has a `recommend_similar` method. If it doesn't exist, you'll need to implement it in the QdrantClient class first.

## 2. Key Technical Concepts

- **MCP (Model Context Protocol)** - Anthropic's protocol for connecting AI to data sources
- **FastMCP** - Python framework with @mcp.tool decorators
- **Agentic RAG** - Agents autonomously choose and chain tools (vs human-directed)
- **Three-backend architecture**: Qdrant (vector DB), Neo4j (graph), Zotero (metadata)
- **Qdrant GraphRAG Figure 1/2/3 patterns**:
  - Figure 1: Pure vector search
  - Figure 2: Paper-level entity linking
  - Figure 3: Chunk-level bidirectional linking
- **Tool specialization vs consolidation** - Key design decision for agentic systems
- **Primitive tools vs workflow tools** - Primitives preferred for agent composition
- **More Like This (MLT)** - Vector similarity search primitive
- **Cost-aware tool design** - Separating expensive operations (10k-100k tokens) from cheap ones (~500 tokens)
- **Graceful degradation** - Tools providing fallback when dependencies unavailable
- **BGE-M3 embeddings** - 1024-dimensional vectors for semantic search
- **Hybrid search** - Dense + sparse vectors with RRF fusion

**New Tool Added:**
```python
@mcp.tool(
    name="zot_get_item_fulltext",
    description="⚠️ EXPENSIVE FALLBACK (10,000-100,000 tokens) - Get complete raw PDF text from a Zotero item.

💡 Try these MORE EFFICIENT options FIRST:
- zot_ask_paper(item_key, question) → Retrieves relevant text chunks for Q&A (recommended)
- zot_semantic_search(query) → Find papers by content/topic
- zot_get_item(item_key) → Get metadata only

✅ Use this ONLY when you need:
- Comprehensive full-paper summarization (entire document context)
- Semantic search failed but you know paper is relevant
- Non-semantic tasks (word count, extract all references, find all equations)
- Complete text export for external processing

⚠️ WARNING: Returns 10k-100k tokens. Cost is 20-200x higher than zot_get_item.

Use for: Complete text retrieval when targeted tools insufficient",
    annotations={
        "readOnlyHint": True,
        "title": "Get Item Full Text (Zotero)"
    }
```

## 4. Errors and Fixes

### Error 1: Wrong Context Assumptions in Initial Assessment

**Problem:** Initially recommended consolidating tools (e.g., three search tools into one) assuming human UI context.

**User Feedback:** "please keep in mind that this is an agentic rag system i.e. the agent chooses which tool or set of tools is appropriate for a given query"

**How Fixed:** 
- Completely revised assessment framework
- Researched agentic RAG best practices via web search
- Analyzed actual code implementation in semantic.py
- Validated that three search tools implement distinct Qdrant GraphRAG patterns (Figure 1/2/3)
- Flipped recommendation from CONSOLIDATE to KEEP SEPARATE

### Error 2: Backend Label Miscategorization

**Problem:** Initially labeled database management tools as "System" and ChatGPT wrappers as "Web".

**User Feedback:** "qdrant only has 3?? and where did the Web ones come from??"

**How Fixed:**
- Investigated tool descriptions carefully
- Discovered `fetch` and `search` are ChatGPT API compatibility wrappers
- Recategorized `zot_get_search_database_status` and `zot_update_search_database` from "System" to "Qdrant"
- Changed "Web" to "ChatGPT Compat"
- Correct count: Qdrant 5 (was 3)

### Error 3: Proposing to Remove include_fulltext Without Considering Fallback

**Problem:** Initially recommended removing `include_fulltext` parameter entirely.

**User Feedback:** "but what if the semantic search tool cant find a given paper or the content, if we remove include_fulltext then there is no other fallback mechanism in place to retrieve the content i need. or am i not understanding something?"

**How Fixed:**
- Acknowledged user's valid concern about fallback scenarios
- Revised recommendation to create separate `zot_get_item_fulltext` tool
- Kept fallback mechanism but made cost explicit in tool name
- Tool name itself signals "expensive operation"
- Added strong warnings in description (10k-100k tokens)

### Error 4: Python Script String Matching Failures

### Error 5: Export Tools Miscategorization

**Problem:** Categorized export tools (bibtex, markdown, graph) as belonging to their source backends (Zotero/Neo4j).

**User Feedback:** "but the export tools are not from the zotero api backend, are they?"

**How Fixed:**

- They fetch from source → transform locally → write to file

- Acknowledged more accurate categorization

```
Here's a detailed breakdown of the ingestion and retrieval pipelines from the GraphRAG documentation:

Ingestion Pipeline (Figure 2):
1. Raw Data: Initial unstructured or structured content serving as the foundation
2. Ontology Creation: 
   - An LLM processes raw data into an ontology
   - Structures entities, relationships, and hierarchies
3. Graph Database (Neo4j):
   - Stores the ontology
   - Captures complex relationships between entities
4. Vector Embeddings:
   - An embedding model converts raw data into high-dimensional vectors
   - Captures semantic similarities
5. Vector Database (Qdrant):
   - Stores vector embeddings
   - Enables similarity-based retrieval
6. Database Interlinking:
   - Graph and vector databases share unique IDs
   - Allows cross-referencing between ontology-based and vector-based results

Retrieval & Generation Pipeline (Figure 3):
1. Query Vectorization:
   - Embedding model converts user query into a high-dimensional vector
2. Semantic Search (Qdrant):
   - Performs similarity-based search
   - Retrieves relevant documents/entries
3. ID Extraction:
   - Extracts IDs from semantic search results
4. Graph Context Retrieval (Neo4j):
   - Provides contextual information
   - Fetches relationships and entities linked to extracted IDs
5. Response Generation:
   - Passes graph context to LLM
   - Generates final response
6. Results:
   - Returns response to user
```

```
  1000→        Args:

  1004→        Returns:

  1007→        # Very conservative estimate: 1 token ≈ 3 chars (large safety buffer)

  1010→        if len(text) <= max_chars:

  1012→

  1014→        truncated = text[:max_chars]

  1016→        return truncated

  1019→        """

  1023→

  1034→            conn = reader._get_connection()
  1035→            cursor = conn.cursor()
  1036→
  1037→            # Get itemID for this key
  1038→            cursor.execute("SELECT itemID FROM items WHERE key = ?", (item_key,))
  1039→            result = cursor.fetchone()
  1040→            if not result:
  1041→                logger.warning(f"Item {item_key} not found in database")
  1042→                return None
  1043→
  1044→            item_id = result[0]
  1045→
  1046→            # Check if this is an attachment

  1049→                FROM itemAttachments ia
  1050→                WHERE ia.itemID = ?
  1051→            """, (item_id,))
  1052→
  1053→            attach_result = cursor.fetchone()
  1054→            if attach_result and attach_result[0]:
  1055→                # This is an attachment, get parent key
  1056→                parent_id = attach_result[0]
  1057→                cursor.execute("SELECT key FROM items WHERE itemID = ?", (parent_id,))
  1058→                parent_result = cursor.fetchone()
  1059→                if parent_result:

  1061→                    logger.debug(f"Resolved attachment {item_key} to parent {parent_key}")

  1066→            else:

  1068→                logger.debug(f"Item {item_key} is not an attachment, using as-is")
  1069→                return item_key
  1070→
  1071→        except Exception as e:
  1072→            logger.error(f"Error resolving parent key for {item_key}: {e}")
  1073→            return None
```
